# loglet

loglet tails your application's log files and ships every line to a collector: the HTTP endpoint, set by `collector_url`, that receives your log lines.

## How loglet avoids duplicate lines

Every 5 seconds loglet writes a checkpoint, the byte offset it has read up to in each file, to `/var/lib/loglet/state.json`. After a restart it resumes from the last checkpoint, so no line ships twice.

## Log rotation

loglet keeps a tail set, the list of files it is currently reading. A rotated file stays in the tail set until loglet reads it to the end, then loglet drops it.

## When the collector is busy

When the collector answers HTTP 429, loglet buffers up to 64 MiB on disk, then drops the oldest lines.

## Install

```sh
apt install loglet
```

Set `collector_url` in `/etc/loglet/loglet.toml`.
